review_notes: I read the whole file and checked every @[simp] and @[simp high] attribute. I also read the downstream uses in SplitTorus/Scheme.lean and RootsOfUnity/Scheme.lean. I did not run Lean, so the competition between rules and the loss of the mapValue/powEnd lemmas to simp is inferred from simp's inner-first, priority-ordered matching. It was not observed. The non-simp status of `schemePointsMulEquiv_multiplicativeCharacterGroup_apply` looks deliberate, since making it simp would loop with `multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv_apply`. I left the `uliftZPowersMulEquiv_*` simp lemmas alone, as they look fine.

findings.excerpt:
multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) p =
      schemePointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) multiplicativeCharacterGroup p
        (ULift.up (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)) := by
findings.problem: The simp lemma expands the canonical unit-valued equivalence `𝔾ₘ(A) ≃* Aˣ` into the general character equivalence for `ULift (Multiplicative ℤ)` evaluated at a lifted generator. That is the heavier form, and it hides the `Aˣ`-valued normal form that the specialised lemmas target. Every specialised simp lemma whose LHS is `multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv (p ≫ …)` then has to be marked `@[simp high]` to beat this generic one. Those lemmas are `…_characterGroupSchemeMap`, `…_powEndGroupSchemeMap`, and the downstream split-torus and roots-of-unity analogues. `multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv_mapValue`, which has the same LHS shape, is left without a simp attribute, so simp would expand its LHS with `_apply` before it could fire. `schemePointsMulEquiv_cocharacterGroupSchemeMap` is also `simp high` in order to fire after this expansion.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv_apply` and keep it as an explicit `rw` unfolding lemma. The proofs here and in downstream files already `rw` with it, so they are unaffected. Then keep `multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv` as the simp normal form. Give `multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv_mapValue` a plain `@[simp]` if desired. Demote the `simp high` markers on the lemmas whose LHS is `multiplicativeGroupSchemePointsMulEquiv (p ≫ …)` to plain `@[simp]`, because nothing competes with them any more.
findings.benefit: Simp normal forms stay in the `Aˣ`-valued `𝔾ₘ` equivalence instead of expanding to the lifted-`ℤ` character evaluation. The priority workaround `simp high` is no longer needed, and the naturality lemma becomes usable as a simp rule. Users avoid rule conflicts when they add further `p ≫ …` lemmas.

findings.problem: The unconditional simp lemma rewrites `(schemePointsMulEquiv G p g : A)` into `(groupSchemePointsMulEquiv G p).ofConv (MonoidAlgebra.single g 1)`. It turns the canonical character-level expression into an expression about the intermediate convolution-point equivalence, and it fires on every coerced character value. No simp lemma goes back from the intermediate form. The sibling lemmas `…_groupSchemeMap` and `…_mapValue` are stated at the `schemePointsMulEquiv` level and are not simp. So after a `simp` call, a coerced value like `↑(schemePointsMulEquiv G p g)` can end up in a form where they no longer apply. The downstream split-torus and roots-of-unity files re-declare their own `schemePointsMulEquiv_apply_coe` and use it only through explicit `rw`.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `schemePointsMulEquiv_apply_coe` and use it explicitly. The downstream uses are all `rw`. Alternatively, keep `schemePointsMulEquiv` as the simp normal form and add simp lemmas for naturality (`schemePointsMulEquiv_mapValue` and `schemePointsMulEquiv_groupSchemeMap`) instead.
findings.benefit: The simp set no longer exposes the intermediate `groupSchemePointsMulEquiv` and `MonoidAlgebra.single` representation. Coerced character values stay in character form, where the naturality and pairing lemmas of the file can fire.
